Using the Tools

A practical guide: begin by making a model subscription useful, complete a real task, then improve your tools and working environment. Read and understand in your native language, entrust investigation, implementation, and maintenance to the model, and revise through use. This guide chooses Mac and ChatGPT / Codex as one concrete route; your existing computer and another available model tool can carry the same work.

Embodied, full-modal learning; embodied, full-modal understanding; embodied, full-modal work—bring them into your life. Develop understanding through text, images, sound, bodily experience, and practical action; turn ideas into works and let the world's response revise judgment. “Full-modal” means drawing on available perception and expression when they serve the task. Models and environments carry detail and repetition while reading, looking, listening, expression, and practice cultivate your sense of the whole, intuition, judgment, and creation.

You can give this page to the model, describe the need at hand, and let it select, configure, and verify useful tools from the map.

This page retains general advice useful to most people. For sustained paper reading, disciplinary methods, experiments, or research writing, continue to Research and Learning.

One route into practice: establish connectivity → use an actually available model subscription → install a local client and prepare basic instructions and necessary Skills → complete one real task → improve tools and the environment through use feedback. The model unfolds search, configuration, adaptation, and necessary implementation around the task, continuing from results that actually work.

You can also go directly to beginning with the model's execution inner loop, ways of learning, working, and living, or automatic collection and environment repair.

1. Device and network: make your existing computer usable

If your computer can run the tools you choose, start there. When choosing a Mac, check the software’s current operating-system and chip requirements. Add memory, storage, or another display when your projects and actual working conditions warrant them.

Your network needs to support sign-in, documentation, dependency downloads, and uploads. When proxy configuration is useful, Clash Verge Rev can manage routes; DuyaoSS provides a community entrance for provider introductions, speed-test records, and routing explainers. Let the model configure for the current network and test sign-in, downloads, and uploads.

When proxy traffic is limited or large software, dependency packages, and Docker images download slowly, ask the model to inspect suitable mirrors and caches. Package sources and Docker image registries are different configuration targets. A directly reachable mirror can reduce proxy traffic, while caching reduces repeated downloads. Docker's registry-mirror documentation describes fetching from upstream when needed and reusing cached content afterward. Check origin, supported packages or registries, synchronization, versions, and integrity information, then test on the current network.

2. From a subscription to global instructions and essential Skills

Web ChatGPT provides a cloud conversation and tool space for discussion, research, understanding materials, and developing ideas. With the relevant access, local Codex can directly help construct and maintain a personal knowledge and working environment: connecting materials, notes, applications, files, scripts, tools, and configuration, and turning ideas into usable arrangements. A project folder is one working location within it; the environment itself can be an ongoing object of improvement. You bring purpose, experience, and judgment; the model carries explanation, investigation, construction, execution, and checking. A concrete need can begin that collaboration.

If you have no usable account, establish connectivity, then choose and purchase a subscription actually available to you. Start on the Web and ask the model to help articulate your purpose and global instructions. Follow the official quickstart to download a local client, sign in, and connect a working directory. An existing local client can also help with these preparations.

Check whether your existing account includes the Codex capabilities, limits, and client you need. The official documentation states that Codex is included in ChatGPT plans; actual capabilities and limits depend on the plan, account, and rollout. Use the sign-in guidance for ChatGPT-account access. Compare an upgrade only after a concrete limit or missing feature becomes relevant.

Choose a stable personal subscription, then compare its practical value

Prefer an individual consumer (ToC) subscription, and put reliability ahead of discounts. Establish account ownership, continued sign-in, the models and usage actually available, and renewal and recovery arrangements. Prefer direct official purchase or a clearly sourced channel with dependable delivery and renewal. Compare business (ToB) team or enterprise plans when you actually need collaboration, organization management, enterprise data policies, or contractual guarantees.

Build everyday collaboration around one stable primary subscription, using its actual included entitlements across the local CLI/app and the Web. Make the arrangement useful before adding or switching subscriptions for a demonstrated capability difference. Frequent switching creates adaptation work for instructions, Skills, interfaces, and habits. Reassess actual needs and value before renewal. Interfaces for a specific purpose, such as translation, can still be configured separately.

Among candidates with adequate reliability and capabilities, assess local and Web use together and use the corresponding models' API prices as a reference for subscription value:

  1. List capabilities you will actually use. Check the models, modes, tools, limits, and reset periods available locally and on the Web. Count shared allowances once.
  2. Estimate the API alternative for comparable work. Where a comparable API exists, estimate monthly input, cached input, output, and necessary tool usage against the provider's current rates. The OpenAI API pricing page, for example, identifies billable categories. Compare Web-only capabilities and hard-to-estimate usage separately by their actual contribution.
  3. Compare the actual monthly fee with work you can reliably complete. Account for local plus Web demand, quality, speed, allowances, and renewal cost, then choose the better value among dependable candidates. API replacement cost supplies a reference for this comparison.

ChatGPT and the API have separate billing. Explore API billing when you actually build your own API application or choose API authentication. Consult current official prices and availability.

Consider Gemini Pro when you use Google tools regularly

If Google Drive, Gmail, and Gemini Notebook will form your everyday materials, email, and learning environment, consider Gemini Pro. It can complement the primary collaboration subscription: the reason to buy includes more convenient storage, email, and source-based learning, as well as another conversational model.

Consider these benefits together using Google's current plan comparison:

  • Storage for files and email: expanded storage shared across Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos, supporting a growing collection of materials, documents, and messages.
  • AI inside Google apps: Gemini in supported applications such as Gmail and Docs can assist with email and documents while reducing the need to move content between windows.
  • Notebook and source research: higher usage limits for Gemini Notebook for source-based questions, organizing materials, and learning formats such as Audio Overviews.

Drive, Gmail, and the notebook tool already offer free functionality; the subscription adds storage, allowances, and applicable AI benefits. Before buying, use the Google account you intend to keep and check its plan benefits, regional and language availability, and actual renewal price. Light use can begin with the free features. If you already need more storage and regularly work with email and research materials, the combined plan is especially worth comparing.

Let the model help establish the working arrangement

Begin global instructions with a few arrangements that apply across your work: how you want to participate, what the model should carry, how native language and English are used, where files and results belong, and how the model completes work and makes it visible. A Web model can help write them; a local model can place them where the actual client reads them and check that they take effect. You provide purposes and corrections; the model maintains the instruction files, and both revise through use.

The author's recommendation is to use simple, globally shared Skills, plugin, and MCP configuration for everyday work, with Full Access as the default for ordinary global work locally. Let the same useful capabilities serve different tasks, retaining local exceptions only when a particular project has a concrete need. The judgment here is that unnecessary constraints may divert work into workarounds, repeated interruption, or maintaining the agent's Harness at the expense of the user's intended result. Make the Harness serve actual work and revise it through concrete problems.

This is the working approach chosen by this guide. Full Access removes the local sandbox and ordinary step-by-step approval prompts; product controls over particular tools and application actions, operating-system authentication, and access granted by service accounts retain their actual mechanisms. It lets the model execute existing-scope work more continuously. Consult the permissions guide and approvals and security guide for the specific meaning.

Ask the model to select, download, and verify the Skills needed now from trustworthy sources. Initial capabilities might cover research, local environment diagnosis, scripts and tools, document reading, interface implementation, versioning, and publication. Choose packages supported by the actual client and check origin, compatibility, and invocation. Agent Skills explains this capability-package format. Globally shared means maintaining reusable capabilities together where the client supports it; what another worksite can actually use still depends on its connected environment.

For graphical management of several clients, CC Switch is an optional choice for provider configuration and the MCP, Skills, and Prompts it supports. It manages client configuration. After a change, let the model read back the client actually in use and confirm that the selected provider, instructions, and tools have taken effect. Continue with an existing simple, maintainable setup when it is sufficient.

Form settings that fit through actual work

Tell the model what you want to do now, where the relevant materials are, and your preferences for language, explanation, responsibilities, and presentation. For example: “Discuss this with me in Chinese, make this material comfortable to read, retain its sources, and check the links.” Working context and preferences can develop task by task. Let the model maintain them in suitable instructions or project notes, and test their fit through use and correction.

For everyday prompts in chat, prefer clear, complete natural language. State what you want accomplished, the relevant background, and important requirements: for example, “Make this report easier to understand, explain key terms, and retain its evidence and sources.” The model can help develop what is still unclear and refine it through actual results.

Yinyang's six actual files and the personal information in personal also use clear accounts suitable for actual work. The six actual files in private references/situated/ are working models of person–model cooperation: orientation, person, counterpart, relationship, environment, and the actual revision method. They select implications needed to make the actual personal environment fit the person psychologically and practically. Psychological and life evidence and maintained interpretations principally belong in references/personal/, with relevant originals retained at their existing owners and reached through its source index. Public writing guides explain how to form the accounts without carrying a particular person's actual accounts. Make the objects described, relationships between concepts, grounds for claims, and conditions of applicability explicit. Distinguish actual information, interpretations, chosen directions, and remaining uncertainty so the model can understand, reason, and participate in actual work. For everyday model-facing text, prefer explicit prompts and contextual explanations. Use philosophy or literature when direct explanation still leaves an important relation unclear, and state its concrete meaning here.

The website's philosophical essays and their source manuscripts can fully develop thought through philosophy and literature, making overall purpose and relationships understandable and perceptible. The model helps construct both corresponding forms: one lets the person understand, judge, and revise arrangements in life; the other lets models build and maintain the environment through explicit accounts, prompts, tools, and configuration. The same understanding takes a different form in each, and actual use can revise both.

Begin tool use by completing a real task and improving the environment through its results. If the background interests you, select Yinyang's methods and material around a question; that reading and the current tool setup serve their respective purposes.

Make Skills discoverable and composable in Chinese

Begin each Skill's description with a short Chinese name and purpose, while retaining its exact native English identifier. You can then express ordinary Chinese intentions and let the model discover, select, read, and invoke suitable capabilities currently available. The Chinese description supports understanding and discovery; the native identifier still supports accurate installation, invocation, and updates.

Distinguish origin with the <用户自制> marker followed by a space, then the Chinese name and purpose. For example: “<用户自制> 资料整理：整理选定材料并保留来源。” This separates origin from “name: explanation”. An external description can read “PDF 阅读：读取和检查 PDF 文档。”. Translation and local adaptation retain the external Skill's authorship. Have the model check the maintained source, description validation, and the client's discovery list together to preserve the format through updates. The marker identifies origin; the native English identifier still supports exact invocation.

Give preference to user-authored methods that fit your purpose, and actively combine related methods as connected working capabilities. They can contribute while understanding a need, configuring the environment, doing the work, and revising the result. Combine suitable external specialists where they help. Priority follows the task, scope, and fit.

Use the available capabilities to complete actual work next. Search for and connect tools when needed, writing a new implementation only when a suitable one is missing. Your working arrangement develops through purpose, use, and feedback.

Know what is available in your environment

Keep a human-readable capability map alongside the configuration a model can find. Explain what each capability does, where to begin, where results go, and which connections already work. Tool names and script paths can supply later entrances; lead with recognizable tasks such as finding readable full-text papers, making a concept interactive, or editing and checking a spreadsheet. Have the model update this explanation as tools change. Forgetting an available capability is also a usability gap.

3. Translation and reading in your native language

First translate needed foreign-language material into your native language, then read and understand it in that language, spending attention on content and relationships. For someone whose native and habitual reading language is Chinese, explanations, navigation, comparisons, progress, and results should normally be in Chinese. Other readers can choose according to their own language and habits. Return to the foreign-language original for key terms, disputed arguments, or unclear passages. Switch reading modes when language practice is your purpose.

  • Long webpages: connect an available translation API to Immersive Translate or Read Frog for bilingual reading. Reduce switching while retaining the original for inspection.
  • Selected text, images, and application interfaces: on Mac, Bob supports selection translation, screenshot translation, and translation displayed over the captured image. Select text when possible and capture it when necessary; the recognition and translation services make separate contributions to the result.
  • Longer documents and courses: ask the model to prepare a resumable reading edition, retaining headings, formulas, figures, code, and sources. Translation supports understanding; important definitions and inferences should remain traceable to the original. Preserve formulas and code accurately.

Choose the reading interface and translation API separately

Bob, Immersive Translate, and Read Frog are reading entrances; another service can perform the translation. Translation can begin with free AI. AIHubMix, OpenRouter, and NVIDIA API Catalog offer free models or trial access to examine. Tell the model: “Choose a currently usable free translation endpoint, connect it to my reading tool, and translate a real passage.” Let the model check current activation conditions, model availability, and integration details and carry out the configuration.

Free options are worth trying for occasional words and passages. Whole pages, many consecutive pages, or large document collections generate more requests and are more likely to meet rate limits, waiting, or exhausted allowances. Ask the model to reduce concurrency, retain translations already produced, or compare inexpensive paid endpoints and available subscription capabilities when sustained volume matters. OpenRouter's limits documentation and current provider pages support configuration checks. The price of the reading interface and the price of its model are separate questions.

Another route connects an existing model subscription through a gateway or proxy you manage, exposing a compatible API to translation tools. Sub2API provides subscription-quota access, upstream routing, and client-key management. CLIProxyAPI (CPA) provides OpenAI-, Gemini-, and Claude-compatible endpoints and supports upstream access such as Codex OAuth. Select a suitable implementation for your existing account and the protocols your translation tool actually supports. This connects upstream capabilities to a suitable Bob plugin, Immersive Translate, or Read Frog, consuming the corresponding subscription or service allowance. CC Switch above manages client configuration; these gateways handle requests and routing. Their purposes connect while their functions differ. Select according to upstream terms and actual account conditions.

Let the model align endpoint, authentication key, model name, and protocol. Use a browser extension's OpenAI-compatible settings when supported; in Bob, choose a service or plugin that supports the endpoint. Test a short passage, then inspect long-page segmentation, speed and limits, and screenshot text recognition. Keep keys in a password manager or the application's credential storage, with placeholders and explanations in shared configuration.

For example, Bitwarden CLI can manage passwords, API keys, and access tokens: retain credentials in the vault and let tools retrieve the relevant item through the command line when needed. Ask the model to configure and verify this retrieval path. Public files keep item references, placeholders, and usage notes; actual secret values remain in the credential system. Access to vault data needs a valid authenticated and unlocked session, arranged for the actual environment.

The person's reading language and the model's working language can differ. This guide uses the following arrangement: human-facing material uses the person's native language; technical notes, handoffs, and tool instructions primarily maintained by models default to English. English documentation, terminology, and interfaces make that arrangement convenient. Adjust the arrangement according to actual results. Preserve the required language and format of sources, quotations, code, paths, and interface fields. Present the final explanation in the reader's language.

You can tell the model: “Discuss the work with me in my native language, including the results, evidence, and choices I need to judge. Use English by default for technical material that another model will maintain. Preserve originals, code, and identifiers accurately, and explain any English passage I need to understand where it appears.” Translation services may send selected text or screenshots to the configured provider; choose handling for private material according to its actual destination.

To understand how a tool actually behaves now, prioritize recent community Issues, PRs, and use reports that identify versions and provide reproducible steps. Resource access and conditional judgments about unauthorized copies

The legitimacy of a resource needs more than a paid-versus-free distinction. Author-posted manuscripts, open-access papers, public-domain works, openly licensed material, and library resources have their own access and use conditions. Ask the model to locate a suitable version and check its content, source, and intended use. WIPO's copyright FAQ introduces the distinctions between permission, the public domain, and exceptions.

Anna's Archive and Sci-Hub can also enter your assessment of resource channels. The former aggregates records for books and papers, while the latter focuses on scholarly articles. These sites involve unauthorized copies and copyright disputes, so assess particular material under the conditions below. Domains and accessibility change; consult the background and entry information for Anna's Archive and Sci-Hub, and verify the current source.

For material suspected of circulating without authorization, availability, financial circumstances, private study, and effects on creators can enter an ethical discussion. Assess ethical questions through the circumstances and permitted use through the applicable authorization. Reading, retaining a copy, redistribution, and commercial use are different acts; assess the particular resource's permissions and applicable rules, and preserve attribution. Software also raises questions about executable origin and integrity: prefer trustworthy open-source alternatives, trials, or educational access.

5. Make tools that fit the person

The purpose running through these arrangements is to control complexity. Judge an arrangement by whether it reduces the burden of understanding, operation, and maintenance while retaining the capabilities you need.

One related software-engineering idea is a small, simple interface carrying deep, rich functionality. John Ousterhout's book A Philosophy of Software Design connects interface complexity, functionality, and information hiding. In a personal environment, “prepare reading material for this book” can be the person's entrance while the model locates editions, converts, organizes, and checks them. Sources, results, and consequential choices remain inspectable. “Small” concerns the operations and conventions a person must master. Put complexity where it can be handled while keeping important choices visible.

The goal can be to entrust construction and maintenance of the whole daily working environment to the model: install and configure software, organize material, build tools, repair faults, maintain instructions and Skills, and connect the changes to daily use. The person primarily expresses purposes, reads, judges, and responds, writing only necessary Markdown. The model carries the remaining documents, code, configuration, and maintenance. It needs a clear work scope, usable tools, and resumable records; personal decisions such as purchases, identity verification, and publication remain governed by actual authorization.

Design separate entrances for the person and the model. The person needs native-language labels, clear hierarchy, clickable titles, and visible state and results. The model may work better with command-line interfaces, structured data, explicit tool contracts, and maintenance notes. Both entrances address the same work, with a maintained source. Let the model connect tool choices and repeated steps it can resolve; present the choices that actually need human purpose, judgment, or authorization.

Configure search first and prefer existing tools

Use a hack-oriented approach of combining and adapting existing tools. Give the model working web and GitHub search and documentation access, verified with a real query. For a new need, first look for an existing implementation and inspect its documentation, recent maintenance, and user reports. Let the model install and configure it, arrange appropriate update checks, and adapt it through settings, plugins, small patches, or rewriting when necessary. Write a new implementation only when no suitable one exists. After updates, verify that the original work still succeeds and retain a recoverable version.

Several concrete search tools can be combined by purpose:

  • General web and source discovery: Brave Search searches webpages, news, and other information; Parallel, Exa, and Tavily offer search and information access for model use. Let the model select by source coverage and actual results.
  • Page reading and bulk extraction: Firecrawl reads pages, crawls sites, and extracts content. Discover the relevant object, then inspect the original. For recent community discussion, an available Last30Days integration can collect evidence across sources using a time range chosen for the question.
  • Papers and academic material: Consensus, SciSpace, and Hugging Face Papers are possible entrypoints, with Hugging Face Papers particularly close to the AI research ecosystem. Return to the paper, author, or publisher to check the original research.

Use an existing client's native search when sufficient; add a relevant plugin, MCP connection, or API when coverage, full-text access, or specialist sources are missing, and verify it with a real query.

Get and manage Mac applications

On a Mac, prefer Homebrew for applications it distributes and updates. For a graphical interface, Applite lets you browse, download, install, update, and uninstall Homebrew applications. If Homebrew is already installed, have the model check which installation Applite uses and connect it to the existing management arrangement.

MacKed is another place to find Mac applications and download resources. It is a third-party site that includes cracked software; assess each application's source, authorization, and executable integrity separately. The resource-access discussion above applies here as well.

Use other people's GitHub repositories

Give the model the repository link and the outcome you want. Have it read the README, installation instructions, license, and supported platforms before choosing an entrance:

  • Use a released tool: when the project supplies application installers or Releases, select the version for your operating system and processor. Command-line tools may instead use Homebrew, pip, or npm. GitHub's download guide distinguishes source snapshots from clones with history.
  • Run or study the source: to run source code, inspect implementation, or keep following updates, have the model clone the repository, prepare documented dependencies and configuration, and verify an example with real input.
  • Adapt it to your needs: first judge whether configuration, a plugin, or a small patch is enough; fork when you need to maintain your own remote version. Keep the reason for changes, the upstream source, and a recoverable version. Compare local modifications with upstream changes during updates, resolve conflicts, and verify the result again.
  • Ask, contribute, and reuse: search existing Issues and documentation first. For a reproducible problem, collect the environment, steps, and result in an Issue; propose improvements through a PR. GitHub's contribution guide describes this path. The model can use GitHub CLI or a connected GitHub tool where useful, posting under your actual authorization. A repository may also supply papers, documentation, Skills, templates, or implementation ideas; its license determines the permitted copying and adaptation.

Connect actions with scripts, Hooks, Skills, and interfaces

A setting, direct link, or short script may be sufficient. When a method needs repeated use, access across projects, or distribution to others, choose an appropriate package:

  • Small script: connect concrete actions, such as turning materials into a linked reading page, providing a clearly named menu for common actions, or displaying a background task's completion and errors. The human entrance can be a button, menu, or webpage while the model maintains execution details.
  • Hook: connect an action to a defined event, such as checking formatting before a commit or recording a result afterward. Where a client exposes the relevant events, a Hook can also organize tool output or display a task-completion notification. Git hooks are one concrete example. Events, inputs, and failure handling belong to the actual host. Have the model connect the existing entrypoint, trigger a real event, and inspect the result.
  • Skill: describe a recurring task's purpose, method, required material, and checks in a capability package the model loads when needed. Agent Skills can include instructions, scripts, references, and templates. Their value is making the next task resumable.
  • MCP: use Model Context Protocol when a model needs a stable interface to a data source or operation. Examples include querying a reading catalog, reading selected notes, or calling an existing conversion program. Configure the needed service connections and read/write capabilities.
  • Plugin: where the selected client supports it, package related Skills, tool connections, and resources for installation, discovery, and updates. Packaging depends on the client.

In the unified ChatGPT and Codex plugin directory, install a needed capability through Plugins, connect the corresponding service when needed, and use it in a new chat. Installation makes a package available; a service connection gives the account access to its materials and operations. Check in the actual conversation that the required tools are present. The Google Drive plugin covers Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides. A GitHub connection can provide repository, Issue, and PR tools, with actual reading and writing determined by service authorization and the current interface.

Custom capabilities can work alongside these native connections: a Skill explains how to approach a kind of work, an MCP server supplies actual data and operations, and a plugin organizes related parts into an installable capability. The model can combine them for research, document changes, or code collaboration, using the interfaces actually available in the current client and worksite. Have it check the result through a real read or modification needed by the current task.

Other practical tool ideas include: turn PDFs into readable material while preserving formulas and sources; connect selection translation to the current reading action; replace hard-to-remember commands with a searchable menu; link works, originals, and versions directly; and report meaningful background completion or failure while preserving the person's current window, input focus, and work.

Generate images, explain with diagrams, and edit images

Let the model select the visual form for the actual question. Image generation can produce illustrations, characters, atmosphere, and visual alternatives from a description; inspect whether exact numbers, relationships, or wording retain their meaning. Visual explanation can use Archify for explorable architecture, process, and state diagrams, and Diagram Design for concepts, comparisons, and relationships. Interactive pages can let readers change conditions and observe results. These tools and methods have their own upstream maintainers, instructions, and licenses.

Editing an existing image can use PhotoCraft: have the model open the selected image, inspect available operations, edit, preview, and export. Generating an image, explaining a relationship, and editing an original serve different purposes. Choose through what you need to understand or create. For study material, place key objects, arrow meanings, conditions, and source support beside the diagram so it contributes to understanding.

Organize work across life with Skills and Projects

This approach can serve many areas of life: psychological exploration and organizing experience, shopping comparisons, coursework, preparing for medical appointments and reading medical material, work projects, game setup and guides, exercise records and plans, and music listening, recording, and practice. Different domains need different knowledge, evidence, and professional support. A model can help select and develop suitable methods, then connect the tools actually available.

A Skill preserves a reusable method, a Project organizes a continuing purpose with its materials and results, and tools perform concrete operations. A shopping Skill can serve different purchases, while a continuing study Project retains courses, progress, and exercises. 7. Begin with the model's execution inner loop

You express a need, and the model investigates, constructs, executes, checks, and revises. The result enters actual use, and you and the model reconsider the need through experience and consequences. Use outer loop: express purpose and experience → encounter and use results → judge together, respond, and redirect.

Execution inner loop: the model understands the task → investigates conditions → constructs and executes → checks the result → revises until usable.

“Inner” and “outer” depend on the chosen system boundary. The execution inner loop includes tools, actual runs, and result feedback. Inner and outer loops are familiar structural terms in control engineering. Here they describe feedback layers in human–model collaboration.

The first execution inner loop can address an actual need: connect translation, prepare global instructions, use a Skill, make material readable, or improve a frequent operation. It can also produce a course page, investigate a question, organize work, or establish a repository. When your experience, authorization, or personal verification is required, the model returns that concrete question.
  3. The model preserves resumable results. Relevant material, configuration, and versions stay in their proper places, ready for subsequent work.
  4. You use and judge; the model revises. Point out friction, omissions, and misunderstandings for the next iteration. Your feedback can also redirect work already underway.

Through these loops, working preferences, environment, works, GitHub repositories, model settings, Skills, and custom tools can evolve together.
